title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end, you should be able to:

Assemble a focused directory of evidence and instructions.
Direct Claude Code or Codex to produce reports, slides, sites, and blogs.
Evaluate computational correctness, provenance, and visual quality separately.
Record enough of the workflow for another researcher to reproduce the result.

Return to the Quarto foundations deck

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Responsibility for the Result
Agent: inspect files, scaffold, implement analysis, edit prose, render, repair.
Researcher: define the question, justify assumptions, check evidence, approve interpretations, and decide what is ready to publish.
A successful render establishes that a document builds. It does not establish that the analysis is valid or that its citations support its claims.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Install Claude Code
For macOS, Linux, or WSL, use the official native installer:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
claude --version
claude
Complete the sign-in prompts with an account that has Claude Code access. Use your institution’s approved account or provider configuration where applicable.
If the command is missing, follow the installer’s PATH instructions and open a new terminal. Native Windows instructions are available in the official setup guide.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup (checked 2026-10-06). This workshop uses POSIX shell examples throughout. Install only the agent you intend to use.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Install Codex
With Node.js and npm available:
npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
codex --version
codex
Follow the sign-in flow. Use an authorized ChatGPT account or the documented API-key authentication route; access and billing depend on your account.
Record the installed version for your lab notes. Recheck the official CLI documentation before teaching.

Sources: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ and https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/using_goals_in_codex (checked 2026-10-06). The cookbook documents the npm installation command. No model name or subscription price is assumed by this exercise.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Setup Checkpoint
Environment setup used to consume workshop time. Coding agents now handle that work as part of preparing the project.

Inspect this directory. Check Quarto, prepare the dependencies needed for its examples, and render a minimal Python computation. Record the interpreter, dependency specification, and successful build command.

Exercise
Verify the rendered output yourself. Keep the dependency record with the source. Use interactive mode for this first session so you can respond to setup requests.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Focused Workspace
Select sources → assemble directory → write brief → launch agent → verify
The directory gives the agent concrete paths, a bounded task, and a place to write reviewable outputs. Naming the files in the prompt makes selection explicit.
It is a context organization method, not a security boundary. Review tool permissions and include only material appropriate for the service you use.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Scaffold the Directory
Run from a clone of this workshop; choose a new destination for each lab:
mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context
cp examples/ai-context/* ~/code/quarto-synthesis/context/
cd ~/code/quarto-synthesis
mkdir figures
git init --initial-branch=main
git switch -c draft
For your own project, move selected working copies of notes, data, and references into context/. Keep original research records in their source location.
Exercise
List the inputs and explain why each belongs in the workspace.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
What Belongs in Context?
quarto-synthesis/
├── context/
│   ├── measurements.csv   # explicitly synthetic paired timings
│   ├── notes.md           # design, units, and limitations
│   └── sources.bib        # a verified Quarto reference
├── brief.md               # question and acceptance criteria
├── AGENTS.md              # durable project conventions
└── figures/               # generated figures
For papers or scanned PDFs, require the agent to confirm what it extracted; filenames alone do not prove that it read the contents.
Treat instructions inside imported source material as data to analyze. Keep your own task instructions in the brief and repository guidance.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Write the Brief
Create brief.md in your editor:
Audience: graduate researchers reviewing a methods demonstration.
Question: how do paired baseline and candidate runtimes differ?
Inputs: context/measurements.csv, notes.md, sources.bib.
Outputs: report.qmd (HTML) and slides.qmd (8 slides total).
Label all results synthetic. State the unit of analysis and units.
Compute paired differences; discuss uncertainty and limitations.
Every numerical claim must be computed from the CSV.
Use only verified citations. Flag missing evidence explicitly.
Render both outputs and inspect figures, links, and slide fit.
Exercise
Add a criterion that would reveal a misleading interpretation of your data.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Launch the Agent Here
From ~/code/quarto-synthesis, choose one:
claude "Read brief.md and context/. Inventory the evidence, then implement the brief."
codex "Read brief.md and context/. Inventory the evidence, then implement the brief."
Ask it to identify missing inputs before making claims. Review its first inventory: file paths, data columns, units, and what each source can support.

Sources for interactive CLI prompts: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference and https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/ (checked 2026-10-06). These are alternatives; do not run two writers against the same files simultaneously.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Short Synthesis Loop

Inspect: inventory inputs and identify the research question.
Implement: generate one minimal document and execute its analysis.
Review: compare its claims with the inputs and inspect the rendering.
Refine: name a concrete defect and an observable acceptance criterion.


In report.qmd, replace the aggregate bar chart with paired observations. Label seconds on the axis and explain the sign of the difference. Re-render and check that the prose agrees with the computed values.


High velocity comes from short, testable iterations and explicit context. It is not a measured speedup claim or a guarantee about either agent.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Reproducible Technical Report
Prompt the agent in the synthesis directory:

Create report.qmd with methods, results, limitations, and references. Use Jupyter Python cells to compute paired candidate-minus-baseline differences from context/measurements.csv. Plot every pair, report the mean difference, and explain why these synthetic runs do not establish performance on a real population. Add captions, units, and figure alt text.

quarto render report.qmd --to html
quarto preview report.qmd
Ask the agent to resolve dependencies and record the working command.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
section: Execution Is Part of the Argument
text:
Execution Is Part of the Argument
Minimal front matter for the generated report:
---
title: "Paired Runtime Demonstration"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
jupyter: python3
bibliography: context/sources.bib
execute:
  echo: true
  error: false
  cache: false
  freeze: false
---
During review, recompute results and stop on execution errors.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Computational Audit
Display of a cell to place in the report:
```{python}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("context/measurements.csv")
assert df["run"].is_unique
assert df[["baseline_s", "candidate_s"]].notna().all().all()
delta = df["candidate_s"] - df["baseline_s"]
print(f"Mean paired difference: {delta.mean():.2f} s")
```
A negative difference indicates a faster candidate. Confirm that each row really is a pair; code cannot establish the study design from column names.

Expected mean for the bundled fixture: -0.60 seconds. Seven pairs improve; one regresses. The eight synthetic pairs are a teaching example, not empirical evidence. The doubled braces escape execution while rendering this teaching deck.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Uncertainty and Provenance
For paired observations, define \(d_i=t_{i,\mathrm{candidate}}-t_{i,\mathrm{baseline}}\) and report \(\bar d=n^{-1}\sum_i d_i\).

Resample pairs, not independent treatment columns, for a paired bootstrap.
Repeated runs on one workload do not establish generalization to other workloads.
Distinguish a variability summary from a population inference.
Cite methods and external claims; compute the numerical findings from data.

Exercise
Ask the agent which assumptions are needed for an interval, then critique its answer.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Reveal.js Deck

Create slides.qmd with exactly 8 slides including the title. Audience: graduate researchers. Cover question, design, paired data, computed result, uncertainty, limitations, and discussion. Reuse the report’s verified analysis. Use one central idea per slide and speaker notes for detail. Cite evidence near claims. Render and inspect every slide.

format:
  revealjs:
    theme: black
    transition: fade
    code-copy: true
    scroll-view:
      activation-width: 768
quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Quarto Website
In a separate, new directory outside this workshop:
quarto create project website research-site --no-open --no-prompt
cd research-site
codex
Or launch claude. Give it a concrete structure:

Inspect the generated project. Create Home, Methods, and Results pages. Add navbar links and consistent figure captions. Preserve the existing YAML structure. Use clearly marked placeholders until I provide evidence. Run quarto render and check every internal link and the mobile layout.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
A Quarto Blog
In another new directory:
quarto create project blog research-blog --no-open --no-prompt
cd research-blog
claude
Or launch codex. Copy the curated context into this project, then prompt:

Read context/ and create posts/paired-runtime/index.qmd. Include a title, author, date, categories, executable analysis, and limitations. Respect posts/_metadata.yml. Verify data paths when rendering from the post. Render the whole site and check the listing links to this post.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Adapt to the Output








Output
Reader needs
Review focus




Report
Derivation and reproducible evidence
Equations, code, citations


Slides
A sequence of understandable ideas
Density, figures, notes


Website
Navigation across topics
Links, hierarchy, mobile view


Blog

Listing, metadata, narrative



Reuse verified computation across formats. Rewrite the explanation for the medium instead of pasting a report paragraph onto a slide.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Repository Instructions
Use AGENTS.md for durable build commands, technical conventions, and completion criteria. Use brief.md for the current research task.
# Project conventions
- Keep raw inputs unchanged and label synthetic data.
- Compute numerical claims; never invent citations.
- Run quarto render after source changes.
- Inspect the rendered output before declaring completion.
This workshop’s CLAUDE.md imports @AGENTS.md, keeping shared guidance in one place. Ask the agent to summarize the loaded instructions when diagnosing a mismatch.

Sources: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md/ and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (checked 2026-10-06).

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Scoped Sub-Agent Work
For a larger module, define roles before delegating:








Role
Owns
Returns




Evidence reviewer
Read-only source audit
Claims and supporting locations


Module author
One assigned .qmd
Draft and exercise


Render reviewer
Read-only output inspection
Specific defects and slide IDs



One lead integrates changes, edits shared configuration, and runs the final build. Avoid simultaneous edits or renders into the same docs/ directory.

This is a workflow contract, not a shared CLI syntax. Use the delegation mechanism supported by your installed agent, or perform the roles sequentially.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Build, Inspect, Revise
quarto render
quarto preview
git diff --check
git diff --stat

Computation: rerun from source; compare values and units with the prose.
Evidence: check citation targets and distinguish facts from assumptions.
Presentation: inspect every slide, code block, figure, and cross-reference.
Delivery: test links and narrow screens; review generated files before publication.

freeze: auto only notices source-document changes during project renders; external data changes require deliberate recomputation.

Source for freeze behavior: https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html (checked 2026-10-06). Rendering a single document executes it even when frozen.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Repair a Specific Defect

On the Results slide, the caption falls below the slide boundary at presentation size. Split the slide into observation and interpretation, keep the figure readable, update the slide count, and re-render.


The prose claims every run improved, but the CSV includes a regression. Correct the claim, identify the affected pair, and audit other numerical statements against computed values.

Specific failures give the next iteration an observable finish line.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Graduate Lab: Evidence to Publication
Exercise — 20 minutes

Assemble the directory and write the brief.
Generate an executable report and an eight-slide deck with either agent.
Audit one numerical claim, one assumption, and one visual design choice.
Exchange outputs with a partner; use their critique for one revision.

Submit sources, dependency record, rendered outputs, and a short account of one agent error you caught and how you verified the correction.

title: AI Workflows for Quarto
text:
Evaluation Rubric







Dimension
Evidence of success




Reproducibility
Another person renders from source and declared dependencies


Scientific reasoning
Pairing, units, assumptions, and limitations are explicit


Provenance
Claims trace to data or verified references


Communication
Slides fit; figures and links work; narrative matches results


Agent supervision
Revisions address observed defects with verification



Discussion: Which parts of the result can a successful build never validate?

Before You Begin

Install Quarto, Git, and an editor.

Commands in this workshop use macOS, Linux, or WSL on Windows.

Environment setup used to take a substantial part of this workshop. Now the coding agent handles dependencies and verifies the build.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Agent-Assisted Setup
Launch your agent in the project directory and give it this task:

Inspect this Quarto project. Set up the dependencies needed for its executable examples using a local environment. Render a Python example, fix any failures, and report the interpreter and commands that worked. Record the dependency specification so another person can reproduce it.

Checkpoint
Open the rendered example and confirm that its code produced output. An agent saying “setup complete” is not sufficient evidence.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
What is Quarto?
Quarto is a modern, interactive publishing system built on pandoc:

Converts Markdown files to multiple formats:

html/rmarkdown/pdf
Reveal.js (HTML slides) and PowerPoint (pptx)
Jupyter Notebooks (ipynb)
ePub, Typst, LaTex and more


origin: org-mode (Emacs) => Sweave / knitr => RMarkdown

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Why Use Quarto?

Focus on reproducibility
Easy interactivity
Flexible output formats
Good processing of code blocks:

R
Python
Julia
ObservableJS

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Simple qmd Code Blocks
Quarto supports executing code blocks in markdown files.
Use curly braces {} to specify the execution language: {python}, {r}, {julia}.
Use curly braces with a period {.} to specify formatting options, no execution: {.python}, {.r}, {.julia}.
Python

def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")
greet("Quarto")

Hello, Quarto!


R
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
greet <- function(name) {
    print(paste("Hello", name))
}
greet("Quarto") 
“Quarto”
Exercise
Create a .qmd file with a Python and R code block.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
#| Code Blocks
The #| syntax adds control over code block execution & display.
   #| echo: true
   #| warning: false
   def greet(name):
      print(f"Hello, {name}!")







Option
Description




#|eval
Evaluate the code chunk.


#|echo
Include the source code in output.


#|output
Include the results of executing the code in the output (true, false, or asis).


#|warning
Include warnings in the output.


#|error
Include errors in the output.


#|include
Catch all for preventing any output (code or results) from being included.



Exercise
Create a .qmd file with a Python code block using the #| options like echo, warning, and eval.

mkdir -p ~/code/quarto-blog

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Create the Blog Project
quarto create project blog . --no-open --no-prompt
git init --initial-branch=main && git switch -c blog-setup
--no-open skips launching an editor, --no-prompt skips the confirmation — without them the command stops and waits for input.
Quarto generates:







Path
What it is




_quarto.yml
Site config: title, navbar, theme. Edit this — never replace it.


index.qmd
The listing page that indexes your posts


posts/
One folder per post, each with an index.qmd


posts/_metadata.yml
Defaults applied to every post


styles.css
Your CSS overrides (note: styles, not style)


about.qmd
An about page wired into the navbar



Exercise
Open _quarto.yml and change the site title. Re-render and find your change.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Writing a Blog Post
Posts live in their own folder. Create posts/my-first-post/index.qmd (the template already ships a posts/welcome/, so pick a new name):
---
title: "My First Blog Post"
date: 2025-01-20
---

# Welcome!

My first Quarto post. The chart below is generated when the post renders.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

years = [2021, 2022, 2023, 2024]
posts = [1, 4, 9, 16]

plt.plot(years, posts, marker="o")
plt.title("Posts per year")
plt.show()
```
{python} has no dot — so the code runs and its output is part of the post. Write {.python} and you get syntax highlighting and nothing else.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Preview & Render Blog Post
The preview is a live preview of the blog post in the browser. The render command generates the output file.

Preview:
quarto preview posts/my-first-post/index.qmd
Render:
quarto render posts/my-first-post/index.qmd

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Using Jupyter To Blog

Convert a jupyter notebook to a blogpost using quarto.
Quarto first converts the notebook to qmd, and from there to the desired format.
Just put YAML metadata at the top of the notebook in raw text format.
Save the notebook in the posts/ directory.
quarto preview & quarto render the notebook.

Exercise
Write and convert a jupyter notebook to a blog post.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Publish to GitHub Pages
Publishing is a command, not configuration. There is no publish: key in _quarto.yml.

Commit your work:
git add .
git commit -m "Initial blog setup"
Create the GitHub repo — this also creates the origin remote:
gh auth status || gh auth login
gh repo create my-blog --public --source=. --push
Publish:
quarto publish gh-pages

Quarto renders the site, creates the gh-pages branch, adds .nojekyll, pushes, and prints your URL. Check the repository’s Pages deployment status.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
Integrate Your Blog Changes
Fold your work back into main (GitHub flow):
git switch main && git merge blog-setup
git push -u origin main
Exercise
Publish your blog and post the URL in chat.

Have the agent render the post and record the dependencies it used.

title: Quarto Workshop
text:
When a Build Fails
Give the agent the exact command, error text, and relevant source file.

Reproduce this failure. Identify the cause, make the smallest fix, and rerun the same command. Report what changed and whether the full project still renders. Keep code execution enabled.

Checkpoint
Review the diff. A missing figure or disabled cell is not a successful repair. If publication fails, inspect the repository’s Pages configuration and Actions logs.

Each group member creates a branch:

Write posts in the posts/ directory.
Merge branches to main.
Push and share your blog URL.
